key_insight: The paper introduces diffusion-activated epitaxy, a doubly metastable synthesis strategy that enlarges the accessible metastable window and enables discovery of previously inaccessible crystal phases.
engineering_relevance: This approach could accelerate quantum materials discovery by making novel, metastable compounds experimentally accessible through a combined diffusion-and-epitaxy route.
method: Combine two metastable synthesis modes: diffusion and epitaxy.
Systematically explore a narrow synthesis space to stabilize new phases.
Validate products with X-ray diffraction and scanning transmission electron microscopy.
evidence_signal: Within a narrow region of synthesis conditions, the authors stabilized four distinct phases, and three showed XRD/STEM signatures inconsistent with structures in existing experimental and computational databases.
watch_item: The demonstrated phase discovery occurs in a narrow investigated synthesis window, so broader reproducibility and scalability still need confirmation.
paper_title: Doubly Metastable Synthesis for Accelerated Quantum Materials Discovery
